Introduction As airports expand services and electrify their operations, their electric loads will continue to grow. This growth originates from efforts to electrify ground support vehicles, fixed-wing aircraft, and vehicles charging in passenger parking or at rental car facilities [1, 2, 3]. As these site loads grow, the costs to supply electricity across the airport will also increase. These costs may include increases in electricity expenses—through either higher demand charges or variable energy rate structures—or increases in infrastructure costs through site equipment and grid upgrades [4]. However, this growth in costs might be mitigated by leveraging any potential load flexibility or local energy assets. Through appropriately sized on-site power generation and energy storage, as well as the optimization of flexible charging loads with smart charge management (SCM), the Athena project has identified a series of solutions to support growing loads at airports while mitigating the risk of rising electricity costs and avoiding or postponing grid infrastructure upgrades [3, 4, 5].
